result_text:
`all_files.zip` now takes its entry names from the configured aspect names instead of hardcoded literals, so renaming the `buildAndDeployment` aspect no longer stops the zip from being written. The reports module compiles and its tests pass offline, but I did not run a full export with a renamed aspect.

The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`:

- **`all_files.zip` block** (around line 641): the five entries are now built by a new helper from each scope's aspect object, in the same order (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other).
- **New private helper `getAspectFileListEntry`** (just before `getTextDataFolder()`): it derives the file name with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call the loose-file writer uses, and reads that file from the text folder.

With the default configuration the entry names are unchanged. With `buildAndDeployment` renamed, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`, and `git-history.zip` is written again because the exception that used to skip it no longer happens.

I did not change the `catch (Throwable t)` around that block, which is why the failure only showed as a stack trace. Also, `LandscapeAnalyzer.java:283` still hardcodes `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` when it reads per-repository exports; I left it alone because it is outside the export fix, but it will miss the file after a rename. Nothing is committed. I could not read the `git diff --stat` because the shell refused that command.
